overview: Sigma 4.11's Criticals is a six-mode module (Packet, HPacket, Minis, HMinis, Hover, Jump) that injects C04 position packets from the pre-attack event and conditions every crit on the target's hurt resistance. The core doCrits() routine sends y + 0.0626 off-ground, an optional y + 0.0626 + 1e-11 second lift in HPacket mode, and a return-to-ground C04 at the original y that deliberately claims onGround false. Hover mode rewrites the motion event instead: it zeroes lastReportedPosY, lifts y by 1E-8 with onGround true, then decays the lift by 5E-15/4E-15 per tick. Minis and HMinis prepend an onGround-true C06 before a Killaura jump, and Jump mode just calls the real jump(). A HURTTIME setting (default 15) plus ground-tick, step and timer gates decide when doCrits runs.

sections.p: The module subscribes to five event types. EventAttack (pre-attack phase) is the trigger: Packet and HPacket call doCrits() only when the player's own ground checks pass (mc.thePlayer.onGround and MoveUtils.isOnGround(0.001)), the target's hurtResistantTime is at or below the HURTTIME setting (default 15), no step has happened in the last 20 ticks (lastStep.check(20)), either 200ms elapsed or the target is still hittable (hurtResistantTime > 0), the player is collided vertically, and more than one ground tick has accumulated. EventUpdate maintains groundTicks and implements Hover; EventJump prepends the onGround-true C06 for Minis/HMinis on the Killaura setup tick; EventStep resets the step timer and the Hover stage after each step-up; EventPacket zeroes the Hover stage on any S08 teleport and carries a half-written C03 interception that is effectively dead (the HPacket branch inside it is commented out). LongJump and Bhop being enabled blocks the attack path entirely.

doCrits() uses off = 0.0626 - a hair above the classic 0.0625 pixel, per the source comment '0.0625, 17.64e-8' - and sends C04(x, y + off, z, false), then, in HPacket mode, C04(x, y + off + 0.00000000001, z, false), then C04(x, y, z, false). All three claim off-ground, including the return move, so the server's fall distance does not reset at the bottom of the hop. Hover mode works on the motion event: it sets lastReportedPosY to 0 (removing the vanilla moved-too-quickly y reference), claims onGround true at y + 1E-8 on stage 0, then steps y down by 5E-15 and 4E-15 on stages 1 and 2 while claiming off-ground, recycling to stage 0 as soon as y reaches the real position. Minis/HMinis send a C06 at the current position with onGround true during the jump's pre-event so the client can jump even though its previous packets claimed air. Every S08 teleport and post-step event resets the Hover stage so the cycle restarts from the new ground.

The C04s are sent from the pre-attack phase of EventAttack, so they are written to the send queue before Killaura's C02 - the server processes the 0.0626 lift, sees the off-ground return, and the attack that follows registers a crit with roughly 0.06 of fall distance. The hurt-time gating is the module's rhythm: it only crits when the victim's hurtResistantTime is below the HURRTIME threshold (default 15), i.e. when the victim is actually hittable again, which also spaces crits naturally. The groundTicks > 1 requirement forces at least two consecutive grounded ticks before a crit, and the step timer prevents critting out of a step-up. The Hypixel warning posted in onEnable and on every mode change ('Packet criticals doesn't bypass on Hypixel') is Sigma's own acknowledgment that the packet modes are tuned for less aggressive servers; Jump mode (a real jump) is the fallback for those.

files.label: Criticals.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The module is organized around the PACKET mode option and the HURTTIME number setting (lines 36-37). onEnable (line 50) resets stage and count and warns on Hypixel for Packet/Min. EventStep (line 64) resets lastStep and, when not collided horizontally, re-seeds y from the bounding box and zeroes stage. EventUpdate (line 75) counts groundTicks via MoveUtils.isOnGround(0.001), and the Hover branch (line 95) runs when the mode is Hover: it zeroes lastReportedPosY, then per stage lifts y by 1E-8 with onGround true, or subtracts 5E-15/4E-15 while claiming off-ground, recycling when y falls back to the real position. EventPacket (line 120) zeroes stage on S08, counts accepted uid-0 confirmations, and its C03 branch is dead (the HPacket rewrite is commented out). EventJump (line 152) sends the onGround-true C06 for Minis/HMinis on the Killaura setup tick so the client can jump after claiming air. EventAttack (line 164) is the trigger: with the hurt-time, step, timer, collided-vertically and groundTicks > 1 gates it calls doCrits() (line 192), which sends the 0.0626 lift, the optional HPacket 1e-11 second lift, and the off-ground return to y; the Jump mode branch (line 177) calls the real jump() instead.

files.label: MoveUtils.java (ground probe)
files.explanation: The attack gate and the Hover cycle both rely on MoveUtils.isOnGround(height): it ray-casts the player's bounding box downward by the given height and returns true when any collision box intersects - isOnGround(0.001) is a near-perfect ground probe that succeeds while standing and fails as soon as the feet leave the floor by more than a millimeter. The attack gate (line 168) uses it together with the vanilla onGround flag, and the Hover branch (line 98) calls it every pre-update to decide whether to run another lift stage. getJumpEffect() and getSpeedEffect() in the same file are the potion helpers the client's movement modules use.

countering.label: fight.Critical (critical-hit validation)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Critical runs when the server sees a crit (mcFallDistance > 0) and applies three legality rules. The packet modes fail the divergence rule: NCP's own fall accounting (noFallFallDistance, tracked from ray-traced ground) says the player never left the ground, while the server-side fallDistance ticks up from the 0.0626 off-ground claims - the difference exceeds the 1e-5 tolerance while the player is judged on-ground, so data.criticalVL rises and the configured actions cancel the hit. Jump mode fails the jump-phase rule: a crit delivered while sfJumpPhase is between 1 and the lift-off envelope's max phase, with no ceiling above and no block-bounce velocity origin, is illegal because a full jump needs more than six move events - attacking on the first ticks of a jump is exactly what the rule is for. The reset-condition rule also denies crits from water, climbables and slow-fall.

countering.label: Criticals (combat-side vertical check)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Criticals check compares Arc's physics-derived ground state to the vertical speed at each attack: when data.isOnGround() is true and the vertical speed of the current move is below 0.37, the hit is 'critical while onGround'. The 0.0626 doCrits lift is a vertical speed of 0.0626, the HPacket extra lift is 1e-11, and the Hover decays are 5E-15 - orders of magnitude under the floor - while Arc's ground state, derived from LocationHelper ground tracking rather than the packet flag, still reports onGround. Only the Jump mode's real 0.42 jump clears the threshold, and it is handed to NCP's jump-phase rule instead. The module's groundTicks and isOnGround(0.001) client-side gates are irrelevant to a check that recomputes ground from the world.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-jump detection)
countering.explanation: The 0.0626 doCrits hop is a SmallHop signature: wasOnGround, 0 < deltaY < 0.4, prevDeltaY <= 0, no accepted knockback, no slime bounce, no ladder/vine or adjacent solid, and the destination is not really on the ground (the feet sit 0.0626 above the floor) - punish and rubberband. The Hover stage-1/2 decays are sub-tolerance by design, but every Hover stage that moves outside AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally's 0.001 tolerance is caught, and a rubberband mid-cycle zeroes the module's stage through its own S08 handler, resetting the lift. The Mini/HMini C06 with onGround true over air is handled by the ground-truth checks rather than this one.

countering.label: NoFall (ground-spoof family check)
countering.explanation: Grim's NoFall is the ground-spoof family check: on any PLAYER_FLYING/ROTATION packet that claims onGround true without a position change, it ray-casts a 0.001-tall feet box expanded by the movement threshold and flags with setback (10) if nothing collides vertically, rewriting the packet to onGround false. The Minis/HMinis branch is the direct target: it injects C06 packets with onGround true precisely when the player is not on the ground (the source comment says as much - 'if minis criticals is not on ground, send packet onground to be able to jump'), and Grim's isNearGround test answers with the actual block collision. The Hover mode's y + 1E-8 onGround-true claim sits inside the movement-threshold expansion and is accepted; the check only bites on claims that are genuinely airborne, which is exactly the lie the Minis/HMinis C06 tells.
